Description: Unconditional, non-cancellable (or penalty-bearing) purchase commitments for wafers (TSMC is sole source for all <=7nm CPUs/GPUs), substrates, HBM memory, other components and ATMP services. $11.2B due rest of 2026, $22.2B in 2027, $15.4B 2028+. $33.4B is due by end of FY2027. Sized for the MI450/Helios ramp; if AI orders slip, AMD still owes these.
Counterparty: TSMC, memory suppliers, ATMP JVs and other suppliers
Source: AMD Form 10-Q for quarter ended Sept 26, 2026 (commitments note)

Description: Cloud compute capacity commitments: AMD has committed to buy GPU compute capacity from cloud service providers to the extent the capacity is not placed with third-party customers (or capacity AMD reserved to resell). Classic demand backstop for neoclouds; amounts fall as third parties pay. $1.4B due 2027, $1.6B 2028, $1.5B 2029.
Counterparty: Unnamed cloud service providers (neoclouds); reported example: Crusoe
Source: AMD Form 10-Q Q3 2026

Description: Data center lease guarantees: AMD guarantees commercial partners' data-center lease payments, max gross exposure $7.7B with terms up to 15 years; on default AMD may assume the leases. Plus commercial partner debt guarantees (borrowings used to finance data-center infrastructure) of $750M with terms up to 6 months. Total max $8.5B; fair value 'not material', nothing paid to date.
Source: AMD Form 10-Q Q3 2026 (guarantees)

Description: Data center leases signed by AMD but not yet commenced, which AMD expects to assign or sublease to commercial partners: aggregate future payments $13.3B, 10-15 year terms, starting Q2 FY2027. AMD is the head lessee; if partners can't take them, AMD carries the rent. Separately $0.2B of ordinary operating leases not yet commenced.
Counterparty: Data-center landlords; intended sub-lessees are unnamed commercial partners
Source: AMD Form 10-Q Q3 2026 (leases)

Description: Reported backstop of a $300M Goldman Sachs loan to Crusoe to buy AMD chips for an Ohio data center (built by Brookfield-backed 5C); AMD agreed to rent the chips back if Crusoe can't find customers, cutting Crusoe's rate to ~6%. Likely already captured inside the 10-Q cloud-capacity or partner-debt guarantee figures, so not added to the total.
Source: Reuters: AMD to backstop $300 million Crusoe loan, The Information reports

Description: Anthropic: July 2026 hardware supply agreement for up to 2 GW of Helios/MI450 racks (Anthropic expects >$20B spend if it takes the full initial capacity, from 1H 2027). AMD committed to buy up to $5.0B of Anthropic Class N stock, drawn by Anthropic in increments as GPU delivery milestones are hit. $2.5B (33.8M shares) bought in the IPO concurrent private placement at $83 (closed after Nov 19 IPO); up to $2.5B more tied to future deliveries. AMD is funding a customer that buys its chips.
Source: AMD/Anthropic partnership release; Anthropic S-1/A via TIKR & Observer

Description: Broader equity investment commitments of up to $5.1B (primarily private AI companies, through FY2028) per 10-Q; likely includes the Anthropic $5B commitment (so not double counted). In addition AMD invested $1.0B in an unnamed public company's equity offering in October 2026.
Counterparty: Privately held AI/tech companies (incl. likely Anthropic); one unnamed public company
Source: AMD Form 10-Q Q3 2026 (commitments)

Description: OpenAI: 6 GW multi-generation Instinct GPU agreement (first 1 GW MI450 from 2H 2026; est. >$100B revenue over ~4 years). AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160M AMD shares at $0.01, vesting per GW purchased and AMD price targets up to $600. Effectively paying the customer in AMD equity to buy AMD chips (vendor financing via equity). TensorWave separately signed a 6-yr, 457 MW AMD-based capacity deal serving OpenAI (Nov 2026).
Source: AMD 8-K: OpenAI warrant

Description: Meta: 6 GW agreement (custom MI450-based GPU, first GW shipping 2H 2026; Reuters: up to $60B over 5 years) with an identical 160M-share $0.01 warrant. Combined OpenAI+Meta warrants = up to 320M shares (~17% of ~1.63B diluted shares). As of 9/26/26 no tranche vested; warrant liability $1.2B on balance sheet, $4.5B unrecognized grant-date fair value to be booked as contra-revenue as sales occur; Q3 took a $1.2B non-cash remeasurement charge.
Source: AMD 8-K (Meta warrant) and AMD 10-Q Q3 2026 (warrant accounting)

Description: Data Center is 64% of revenue (vs 47% a year ago). AMD's 2027 plan (>80% revenue growth guided per reports) leans on three anchor AI customers: OpenAI (6 GW, cash-burning, vendor-financed by AMD/Nvidia/Broadcom), Meta (6 GW) and Anthropic (2 GW, AMD-funded). 10-Q: 'a small number of customers will continue to account for a significant part of our revenue and receivables'. No customer % disclosed.
Counterparty: OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Microsoft, Oracle, neoclouds
Source: AMD Q3 2026 earnings release & 10-Q

Description: Export-control exposure: Hunterbrook short report (Nov 19) alleges AMD firmware reached blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT; new US license rule (Nov 19) for advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Brazil (Singapore was ~12.4% of 2025 revenue by billing). AMD previously took ~$800M MI308 charge (Q2 2025). AMD denies wrongdoing.
Source: The Globe and Mail / Reuters: AMD shares dip as report says China ties could invite U.S. scrutiny

Description: Leases signed but not yet commenced (mostly datacenters/logistics): $2.6B in Q4-26, $12.4B 2027, ... $114.8B thereafter.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q, commitments table

Description: Unconditional purchase obligations for long-term agreements to acquire property and equipment (servers, chips, datacenter equipment); $63.9B due in 2027 alone. Not on balance sheet.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q, commitments table

Description: Other unconditional purchase obligations: energy procurement (take-or-pay style), digital media content, software licenses.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q, commitments table

Description: Other commitments: asset retirement obligations, content liabilities, rent/tenant improvements on build-to-suit leases under construction. Excludes ~$7.3B of tax contingencies.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q, commitments table

Description: Anthropic investment: $8.0B convertible notes (2023-2025) + $5.0B Series G (Q2 2026) + $5.0B Series H (Q2 2026) = ~$18B cost; now carried at ~$238.7B ($146.2B notes FV + $92.5B preferred). Anthropic IPO priced $83/share on 2026-11-18 (~$1.5T valuation).
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q

Description: Committed financing facility to Anthropic, up to $15.0B remaining (originally $20B), unlocked as AWS delivers compute milestones; Anthropic draws at its discretion via convertible notes or stock; expires 30 months after liquidity event. Classic supplier-funds-customer structure.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q

Description: OpenAI investment: $50.0B of Series C Preferred ($15.0B Q1 + $13.7B Q2 + $21.3B Q3 2026), fully funded; recorded as non-equity-method private investment (Level 3).
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q

Description: OpenAI AWS commitment: original $38B (Nov 2025) expanded by $100B over 8 years in Q1 2026 (~$138B total), incl. ~2GW of Trainium capacity -- concurrent with Amazon's $50B investment in OpenAI.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q; Chain Store Age

Description: Anthropic committed >$100B to AWS over 10 years (Apr 2026, up to 5GW); Anthropic S-1 reportedly shows $110B committed to AWS through 2036 -- concurrent with Amazon's $5B + up to $20B investment.
Source: TIKR (citing CNBC reading of Anthropic S-1); Anthropic announcement

Description: AWS backlog $578B (6.1-yr avg life). OpenAI (~$138B) + Anthropic (~$110B) commitments = ~$248B, i.e. roughly 43% of backlog if fully included (our arithmetic; Amazon does not disclose the split). Both labs received Amazon equity funding. Anthropic is also building its own datacenters ('Anthropic Direct' via Fluidstack), capping future AWS share.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q; TIKR

Description: Standby letters of credit assigned to specific beneficiaries.
Source: Amazon Form 10-Q

Description: Unconditional purchase commitments, mostly inventory (TSMC wafers, HBM, packaging, rack components for XPU systems): $52.7B due FY2027 and $73.0B FY2028 - almost all within two years. Sized to the AI order book; if customers (or their SPV lenders) pull back, Broadcom still has to buy.
Source: Broadcom Form 10-Q for fiscal quarter ended Aug 2, 2026

Description: Other contractual commitments (non-inventory), multi-year.
Source: Broadcom Form 10-Q FQ3 2026

Description: AI XPV Platform 'Backstop' (June 2026, $35B Apollo/Blackstone financing): an SPV buys Broadcom-designed AI racks (incl. Google TPUs) and leases them to Anthropic for >1 GW at Fluidstack sites over 5 years. If the customer defaults, Broadcom owes the gap between 85% of the outstanding lease and the racks' resale value. Max undiscounted exposure ~$29B once all racks are deployed; fair value booked as 'not material'.
Source: Broadcom Form 10-Q FQ3 2026; Broadcom/Apollo/Blackstone AI XPV release

Description: 'Project North Star' (Oct 26, 2026): $63B SPV financing (BofA, Citi, Morgan Stanley first lien ~$42-43.5B at SOFR+150/187.5bp due 2033; Blackstone-anchored ~$18B junior, unguaranteed, >10% yield) to buy Broadcom XPU racks leased to Anthropic, deliveries from 2027. Broadcom gives residual value support equal to the first lien: it pays the gap between 72.5% of the outstanding lease and the racks' sale value. Max undiscounted ~$43B, amortizing to zero over 5 years. Reported that CEO Hock Tan stepped in to get banks to finish the deal.
Counterparty: Anthropic (lessee) / North Star SPV senior lenders
Source: Broadcom Form 8-K Item 2.03 (Oct 27, 2026)

Description: Commitment to buy up to $42B of Anthropic convertible promissory notes, proceeds usable only to pay rent on the Broadcom equipment leases; 9% PIK interest (13% if revenue conditions missed), convertible into Anthropic Class N stock at 90% (85%) of 30-day VWAP; assignable to a financial partner. None issued as of 8/2/26. Economically overlaps with the lease rent that services the SPV debt, so not added to the total.
Source: Broadcom Form 10-Q FQ3 2026; Anthropic S-1 terms via AI Stock Wire

Description: $1B purchase of Anthropic Class N (non-voting) stock in the concurrent private placement at the $83 IPO price (Nov 2026), alongside Google, Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Micron and TSMC.
Source: Observer: Anthropic record $81B IPO; seven firms buy $26B in placement

Description: Reported talks (WSJ/Bloomberg, Oct 7-9) for Broadcom to arrange $30B-$50B+ of financing (Apollo, Blackstone) for OpenAI's 10 GW custom-accelerator 'Nexus' program (deployments 2H 2026-2029). Preliminary and unconfirmed; would likely add another residual-value backstop. Not in total.
Source: Yahoo Finance/Proactive: Broadcom seeks more than $50 billion to finance OpenAI AI chips

Description: One distributor = 50% of FQ3 net revenue (32% a year ago); top five end customers ~55% of FQ3 revenue (40% a year ago). Six XPU customers incl. Google, Anthropic, OpenAI. Anthropic has ~$161.2B of 5-year Broadcom equipment lease rent in its S-1 and is expected to become Broadcom's largest XPU customer; Anthropic's own credit is guided to 'high double-B' (sub-investment grade).
Counterparty: Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and other hyperscalers
Source: Broadcom Form 10-Q FQ3 2026

Description: Round-trip structure: Broadcom sells racks to SPVs, guarantees the SPVs' senior lenders via residual value support, may lend Anthropic the rent via convertible notes, and owns Anthropic equity. Broadcom's 'AI XPV' platform targets >20 GW for Anthropic and OpenAI through 2028, so these structures are meant to scale.
Counterparty: Anthropic, OpenAI, Apollo, Blackstone, bank lenders
Source: Broadcom, Apollo, and Blackstone establish AI XPV Platform

Description: Executed leases (primarily data centers, equipment, offices) not yet commenced; estimated future undiscounted payments; commence 2026-2029, terms 7-17 years. Up from $35.5B at June 30 and $38.5B at Dec 31, 2025.
Counterparty: Data-center landlords/developers (not named; includes AMD-related leases ~530 MW signed July 2026)
Source: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026 (StockTitan filing summary)

Source: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026, via sec-api.io / Filing Insights

Description: Committed future data-center construction costs ($2.1B) plus ~$4B of other enforceable purchase commitments (technology equipment, software/services). Separately ~$4.5B of equipment purchases sat in accrued liabilities (on balance sheet).
Source: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026 contractual obligations (listed.markets); Filing Insights

Description: Unconsolidated VIEs/joint ventures: maximum exposure to loss ~$1.9B (JV) plus a VIE-lessor lease with $1.2B committed payments (already within lease figures). DDTL 5.0/5.5 SPV loans carry unconditional parent guarantees (on balance sheet).
Source: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026 (Equibles; Filing Insights)

Description: Nvidia (key/sole GPU supplier) bought $2.0B of CoreWeave stock in Jan 2026 (22.9M shares at $87.20) and holds roughly 10-11%; CoreWeave spends most of its $37-39B capex on Nvidia systems. CoreWeave is the RECIPIENT of this vendor support.
Source: Yahoo Finance: Nvidia is CoreWeave's key sole supplier and $6.3B backstop

Description: Nvidia capacity backstop: Sept 2025 order (initial value $6.3B) obliging Nvidia to buy CoreWeave's residual unsold capacity through 2032-04-13, subject to delivery/service conditions and termination for breach or insolvency. Supports lender confidence; worth ~$1B/yr vs ~$3.4B+/yr interest run-rate. Nvidia interim CEO said (Nov 2026) it will be more selective on future guarantees; existing commitments unchanged.
Source: Yahoo Finance: 'Stay away from CoreWeave' - Huang scandal puts Nvidia's $6.3B backstop in focus

Description: OEM/equipment-maker financing ($6.9B recourse + $0.8B non-recourse) - suppliers lending CoreWeave money to buy their servers; $1.5B of equipment payables were converted into OEM debt in 9M 2026 without cash moving. On balance sheet as debt (not added to off-balance total).
Counterparty: Server OEMs (e.g., Dell) - not individually named
Source: 06.ai W.117 (10-Q debt table); Filing Insights

Description: Two unnamed customers were 30% and 24% of Q3 revenue (top customer 67% a year earlier; Microsoft was 67% of FY2025 revenue). Named commitments: OpenAI up to ~$22.4B cumulative (latest order $6.5B through May 2031), Meta ~$14.2B (to Dec 2031) + ~$21.0B (to Dec 2032), Jane Street ~$6B. >50% of backlog tied to a single contract. OpenAI is itself vendor-financed (Nvidia equity).
Source: CoreWeave 10-Q Q3 2026 risk factors (listed.markets); Inside Deep Tech

Description: Nvidia is supplier, shareholder, customer (renting capacity) and backstop for CoreWeave, and also an equity investor in OpenAI, a CoreWeave customer. Nvidia equity/backstop -> CoreWeave borrows against GPUs -> buys more Nvidia GPUs.
Source: Luminix: Circular Financing in AI

Description: Expected ~$9B of customer prepayments/deposits over the following three months (>$3B tied to recontracting paid-off infrastructure). Funds capex but creates a delivery obligation; converts financing risk into execution risk.
Source: TechTimes: CoreWeave Q3 - $9B customer prepayments expected

Description: Multi-year non-cancelable commitments for technical infrastructure & inventory, energy take-or-pay contracts and content licenses (remaining term >1 yr). Total material purchase commitments are $924.4B incl. open POs; $213.4B due within 12 months; significant majority fulfilled through 2031. Includes third-party compute capacity Google began renting late Q3.
Source: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Purchase Commitments / Note 10

Description: Future lease payments for leases signed but not yet commenced, primarily data centers and energy infrastructure; terms 1-26 years, commencing 2026-2031. Includes leases with data center leasing VIEs (finance leases).
Counterparty: Data center developers / energy infrastructure lessors
Source: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 4

Description: Credit derivatives: Alphabet backstops third parties' data center lease payments and associated energy costs (e.g., Fluidstack leases at former crypto miners). Notional = maximum potential exposure on default; terms up to 15 years; fair value liability $606M. Google may assume the leases on default.
Counterparty: Data center lessees/landlords (incl. Fluidstack sites at TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8)
Source: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 3 (credit derivatives)

Description: Illustrative components of the data-center backstop book: Google backstops Fluidstack lease obligations at TeraWulf Lake Mariner (~$1.8B original + ~$1.3-1.4B for 168MW JV, ~$3.1-3.2B total; Google holds warrants for ~14% of TeraWulf) and at Cipher Mining Barber Lake (total $1.73B). Presumed included in the $48.0B notional above; not summed.
Source: TeraWulf & Cipher press releases; Startup Fortune

Description: Financial guarantees supporting counterparties' procurement of long-lead equipment for future power purchase / energy agreements; terms through Jan 2049.
Source: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 10

Description: TPU hardware repurchase guarantees: certain TPU system sale contracts require Google to buy back previously sold TPU hardware under specified conditions. Company says counterparties lack economic incentive to exercise.
Counterparty: TPU system buyers (undisclosed; likely AI labs/neoclouds)
Source: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 10

Description: Crux AI JV with Blackstone (formed May 2026, announced Q3): Google committed to provide future data center and energy infrastructure backstops of up to $10.0B for agreements the venture enters into; Blackstone commits up to $5.0B of capital. Google holds minority equity-method stake (unconsolidated VIE). May partly overlap with credit-derivative notional once used; not summed.
Source: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 3

Description: Crux AI round trip: Google backstops the JV's data center agreements (up to $10B) AND the JV signed a multi-year commercial agreement to buy from Google, contributing $16.8B to Google's revenue backlog (related-party).
Source: Alphabet Form 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 2

Description: Equity investor in its own major cloud/TPU customer Anthropic: ~$33.3B invested to date (per Reuters calculation), ~13.4-14% stake (cap 14.99%) post-IPO; additionally committed $10B to Anthropic's concurrent private placement at the $83 IPO price (Nov 18, 2026). Stake worth roughly $139-147B at IPO price; large unrealized gains flow through Alphabet's income ($116B of 9M-2026 non-marketable gains).
Source: Bloomberg / Yahoo Finance on Anthropic S-1/A; SmartAsset IPO summary

Description: Anthropic's S-1 discloses at least $121.3B of non-cancelable compute commitments to Google (Apr 2026-Jul 2033, ~$16.7B/yr), ~21.6% of Google Cloud's $560.8B backlog (computed). Anthropic is itself vendor-financed (Google, Amazon, Nvidia, Microsoft investors; ~$900B total compute commitments). Source: Meta Form 10-Q Q3 2026 (Commitments)

Source: Meta Form 10-Q Q3 2026 (VIE note)

Source: Global Data Center Hub: Hyperion financing

Separately, CoreWeave's $8.5B DDTL 4.0 is backstopped by its Meta contract, i.e., Meta's commitments are collateral for neocloud debt.

Description: Meta as a concentrated BUYER of neocloud capacity: CoreWeave ~$35B total (14.2B Sept 2025 + $21B Apr 2026 through 2032); Nebius up to $27B (Mar 2026: $12B dedicated + up to $15B); Oracle ~$20B (Oct 2025); Google TPU rental multi-billion (Feb 2026). Description: Customer prepayments used to fund capex (deferred revenue $9.41B). Q3 contracts' prepayments covered >100% of related capex. These are refundable/penalty-bearing if capacity is late: the Microsoft contract allows termination of affected service after a grace period if delivery dates are missed, plus late-delivery penalties.
Counterparty: Microsoft, Meta, other AI cloud customers
Source: Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending (TechCrunch)

Description: Microsoft: dedicated GPU capacity at Vineland, NJ, ~$17.4B through 2031 (up to ~$19.4B with additional purchases). Remaining tranches slipped to Q2 2027 after site operator DataOne retired temporary generation.
Source: Nebius results: revenue up 571%, and the stock fell 16.8% (citing Nebius 6-K)

Description: Meta: five-year agreement from early 2027 on Nvidia Vera Rubin - $12B dedicated capacity plus commitment to buy up to ~$15B of other capacity (up to ~$27B).
Source: Nebius Group Q3 2026 Earnings SEC filing analysis (sec-api.io)

Description: Three unnamed customers = 33%, 22%, 15% of Q3 revenue (70%); one customer = 75% of accounts receivable ($4.04B AR). RPO $38.7B dominated by Microsoft and Meta.
Source: Nebius Q3 2026 condensed financial statements (6-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Nvidia invests $2B in Nebius -> Nebius buys Nvidia GPUs (Vera Rubin for Meta contract) -> Nebius borrows against those GPUs/contracts. Nvidia also stated it will be more 'disciplined and selective' supporting neoclouds going forward.
Source: Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius: Inside the Circular Financing of the GPU Boom (I/O Fund)

Description: Unfunded 2027 capex: guidance $40-45B with only 75-85% expected from prepayments and asset-backed financing, leaving ~$6-11B to be raised (our arithmetic), on top of refinancing the $3.5B Citi bridge.
Source: Nebius pares back 2026 revenue forecast on capacity delays (Reuters)

Description: Supply and capacity purchase obligations (mainly multi-year memory procurement plus wafer/manufacturing capacity). Up from $279B a quarter earlier and $119B two quarters earlier. $69B due rest of FY27, $203B in FY28, $92B in FY29.
Counterparty: Suppliers (memory makers e.g. Micron/SK Hynix/Samsung, TSMC, others)
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Multi-year cloud service agreements (Nvidia renting compute, often from neoclouds that are also its customers and investees). Includes the CoreWeave residual-capacity order. Company says used for R&D.
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Data center leases signed but not yet commenced, up to 20-year terms, commencing FY2027-FY2033; $63B falls in FY2032+. Some may be assigned to third parties (e.g., reported Beacon Point lease tied to Lambda's Anthropic contract).
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Committed but unfunded equity investments in private companies (AI labs, neoclouds, financiers); $5B rest of FY27, $11B FY28. Likely includes Anthropic IPO placement and Nscale tranche.
Counterparty: AI model makers, neoclouds, other private companies
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Capital expenditure commitments (data center equipment), due rest of FY27.
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Neocloud agreements (formerly 'AI cloud agreements'): neoclouds buy Nvidia infrastructure and Nvidia commits to buy back cloud services (~6-year terms) and shares revenue above thresholds. Conditional on neocloud obtaining financing and Nvidia accepting capacity. Down from $36B in Q2. Separate from the $518B table.
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Credit support guarantees on land, power and shell for ~4.25 GW across nine buildings at SB Energy's PORTS-Pike campus (Ohio), leased for 20 years to OpenAI and exclusively hosting Nvidia infrastructure. Triggered on tenant default; phases in from FY2029 as buildings complete; option for ~3.8 GW more. No payments made to date.
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Power and systems credit support guarantees (hardware/power financing for partners).
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary (8-K Ex. 99.2)

Description: Land, power and shell (lease) guarantees for neoclouds, 5-7 year terms. Includes up to $860.3M guarantee of Nscale's Ward County, Texas lease (in exchange for warrants; $470M of Nscale cash in escrow).
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary; Nscale S-1/A via 06.ai

Description: CoreWeave capacity backstop: Nvidia obligated to purchase CoreWeave's residual unsold cloud capacity through April 13, 2032 (initial order value). Believed to sit inside the $28B cloud service commitments, so not added separately.
Source: Nvidia Is CoreWeave's 'Key Sole Supplier' and $6.3 Billion Backstop (TIKR, citing CoreWeave 8-K)

Description: OpenAI equity: $30B in OpenAI's Feb/Mar 2026 round (replaced the Sept 2025 LOI for up to $100B). OpenAI secured 3 GW inference + 2 GW training capacity on Vera Rubin. Already funded (on balance sheet as investment), but OpenAI is a major indirect buyer.
Source: Nvidia embraces role of AI investor (CNBC)

Description: Anthropic: ~$10B purchase of non-voting Class N shares in the $26B private placement concurrent with Anthropic's Nov 2026 IPO at $83/share (follows Nov 2025 pledge of up to $10B; Anthropic committed to up to 1 GW of Nvidia compute).
Source: Anthropic IPO, Private Placement Close With $119.5B In Gross Proceeds (Forbes Middle East); Reuters factbox

Description: xAI: Nvidia participated in xAI's $20B Series E (Jan 2026), reported up to $2B; xAI later merged into SpaceX and Nvidia now holds SpaceX shares.
Source: Nvidia, SoftBank make final investment in OpenAI (Dealroom, citing Nvidia disclosures)

Description: CoreWeave equity: additional $2B at $87.20/share (Jan 2026); stake ~11.5%. CoreWeave buys Nvidia GPUs and pledges them as collateral; its unsecured bonds yield ~15%.
Source: Nvidia's customer financing is disclosed. Its effect on revenue is not. (The Research Note)

Description: Nebius: $2B for pre-funded warrants/shares (Mar 2026), 9.3% stake (22.26M shares) per July 2026 13G.
Source: Nvidia Reveals 9.3% Stake in AI Cloud Firm Nebius (Moscow Times / Reuters)

Description: Nscale: $2.0B of a $3.36B pre-IPO convertible round ($1.0B notes in Sept + $1.0B closing ~Nov 16, 2026), plus earlier $400M Series B and $777M Series C. Nvidia also rents $1.2B of Nscale capacity (circular).
Source: Nscale loses $1.02bn in six months on the road to a NYSE listing (S-1/A summary)

Description: Lambda: Nvidia leases back ~$1.3-1.5B of GPU servers from Lambda (its customer/investee) and is reported to hold the Beacon Point (Texas) leases that underpin Lambda's $34.9B Anthropic contract.
Source: Which neoclouds depend most on Nvidia? (06.ai)

Description: Three direct customers = 14%, 11%, 11% of Q3 revenue (36%); four direct customers = 13/12/12/11% of 9M revenue (48%). Two direct customers = 18% and 17% of accounts receivable. Hyperscale revenue $60.1B; 'AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise' (neoclouds/labs) $47.5B, up 195% y/y - the segment most tied to vendor-financed buyers.
Source: NVIDIA Third Quarter 2027 Supplemental Financial Information

Description: Extended payment terms to investment-grade customers on multi-quarter deals: AR jumped to $81.0B (DSO 64 vs 45 in Q1), absorbing $18.1B of cash in Q3 - effectively trade credit to buyers.
Source: NVIDIA Q3 FY2027 CFO Commentary; Inside the Latest Quarter (MoatExplorer)

Description: Data-center lease commitments signed but not yet commenced (not on balance sheet); generally commence Q2 FY2027-FY2029, terms 15-19 years. Up from $260B at 2026-05-31. ~6.6x the $43.8B of recorded lease liabilities.
Counterparty: Data-center developers/landlords (e.g., Crusoe/Blue Owl SPVs, Vantage, BorderPlex/Yucca for Project Jupiter); not itemized in filing
Source: Oracle 10-Q Q1 FY2027 lease note, as summarized by FourWeekMBA / 06.ai

Description: Unconditional purchase obligations, primarily cloud infrastructure components and data-center power arrangements.
Counterparty: Hardware suppliers and power providers (not named)
Source: 06.ai W.007 (citing Oracle 10-Q Aug 31, 2026); TradeOnPurpose

Description: OpenAI five-year, ~$300B compute contract (~4.5 GW, Stargate) estimated at ~45% of Oracle's $664B RPO. OpenAI is itself loss-making and vendor-financed (Nvidia $30B equity Feb 2026). S&P and Moody's both cite OpenAI counterparty risk.
Source: Reuters: Oracle says OpenAI infrastructure deal is fully funded; Luminix circular-deals report

Description: Oracle is a RECIPIENT of vendor financing: Investor Day model assumes suppliers finance ~70% of hardware over 5 years (cuts Oracle's cash need for a 1 GW, ~$37B project to ~$18B). Oracle says this financing is 'in place' but has not disclosed size or vendors; it sits in supplier terms, outside the $20B capital-markets cap.
Counterparty: Undisclosed hardware vendors (reportedly incl. chip suppliers such as Nvidia)
Source: Oracle Investor Day 2026 transcript; Oracle X post via The Next Web

Description: Customer prepayments with a financing component: cash received for capacity not yet delivered (~$11.4B in Q1 FY27, ~$4.6B in Q4 FY26; ~$16B liability). Boosts reported OCF now but must be repaid in service, not cash. Separately, prepaid and customer-supplied-hardware ('bring your own chips') deals were said to total ~$75B in June 2026.
Source: ABIS Capital equity research (from 10-Q); StockTitan Investor Day summary

Description: Project Jupiter (Doña Ana County, NM; 2.45 GW Stargate campus for OpenAI): Oracle is anchor tenant of a developer SPV (Blue Owl unit) financed with construction loans and up to $165B of county industrial revenue bonds. Oracle issued a force majeure notice (Sept 2026) over power/permit delays; HSBC sold a ~$300M slice of the construction loan at a steep discount. Oracle's exposure is via lease commitments (included above) rather than a disclosed guarantee.
Counterparty: Blue Owl-affiliated developer SPV; BorderPlex Digital Assets; Yucca Growth Infrastructure; Bloom Energy
Source: Investing.com/Bloomberg: HSBC offloads troubled AI data center loan

Description: Circular loop: Nvidia funds OpenAI (equity) -> OpenAI commits ~$300B to Oracle -> Oracle buys Nvidia GPUs, partly on vendor credit and partly with OpenAI-supplied hardware/prepayments. Oracle's revenue depends on a customer whose ability to pay depends on continued outside funding.
Source: Luminix: Circular Financing in AI
